source_edition.creator: Canada. Census Office / Canada. Bureau du recensement
source_edition.observation: Population as at midnight on 31 March 1901 (Census Act and volume instructions)
source_edition.restoration: Download the PDF and OCR from the exact URLs above, then verify their SHA-256 values; OCR is for discovery only and the transcribed sample was visually checked against the PDF scan.

license_and_access.archive_rights_metadata: No explicit license field or reuse grant in the archive item metadata. Item lists Statistics Canada as contributor and the archive collection includes `statisticscanada`; uploader is Internet Archive.
license_and_access.underlying_work_status: The 1902 publication was produced by the federal Census Office. Canadian Copyright Act, R.S.C. 1985 c. C-42, s.12 states Crown-prepared/published works continue through the year of first publication and 50 years after that year; for 1902 that term would have ended 1952-12-31. This is the basis for treating the underlying publication as public domain in Canada, not a separate license grant from the scan host. No scan images are redistributed here. Jurisdiction-specific reuse of the Archive scan was not independently adjudicated.

evaluated_table.title: Origins of the People by Sub-districts
evaluated_table.table_territory: 1901 Ontario census district 97, Ontario North; source subdistricts a–o on the sampled page
evaluated_table.measure: Population counts tabulated by origin classification, not population share or territory population measurement
evaluated_table.source_observation_bounds: Single census reference moment: midnight 31 March 1901; not a longitudinal interval
evaluated_table.sample_method: Transcribed 15 contiguous subdistrict rows on printed p.336 from the source scan. Only the first seven origin columns are retained; no values are inferred for columns not retained. Source-order names and labels retained. Visual inspection of scan controls transcription; OCR was used only to locate passages.

source_interpretation.origin_instruction: §53 says among whites racial or tribal origin is traced through the father, warns against using American/Canadian as racial terms, names Chinese/Japanese/Negro categories, requests Indigenous tribal names, and describes mixed Indigenous/white categories as “breeds”. Preserve historical vocabulary as source evidence; do not adopt it as an Atlas classification.
source_interpretation.language_instructions: §§65–67 define speaking English/French responses and mother tongue; mother tongue is defined as native language / language of race, not necessarily the language used chiefly. It is a separate schedule field.
source_interpretation.mother_tongue_table_result: The complete volume I table contents list comparative population, population/dwellings, religion, origins/nationalities, birthplace/immigration. No published mother-tongue aggregate table is listed or found in volume I; text defines the schedule variable only. This pass makes no claim about other volumes or unlocated publications.
